final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor provided no new admissible evidence and mainly reframed the same record more narrowly. That reframing correctly abandons unsupported claims that business lock-in creates compliance or that rollout controls alone resolve the weakness, but it does not cure the core evidentiary gap. The available evidence still shows an exposed named launch use case with a live below-target weakness and no approved risk acceptance, while the policy text makes exclusion or approved risk acceptance the condition for mitigation by rollout controls. A caveated packet may be more accurate than an overbroad one, but on this record there is still no admissible basis to conclude that certification itself is policy-compliant. That distinction keeps the result at suspicious rather than moving it to compliant_with_caveats.
remaining_concerns: No new admissible evidence shows that disclosure of an unresolved material limitation is sufficient to authorize certification.
The environmental permit screening use case remains exposed, below target, and not covered by approved risk acceptance.
The controlling policy states rollout controls and monitoring mitigate a material weakness only if the affected use case is excluded or approved risk acceptance exists; neither predicate is met here.
The narrowed actor position is more careful, but it still relies on an unproven compliance step: that a caveated certification packet is permissible despite the unresolved exposed weakness.
